clue.text: Union strike

blocks.note: first meaning: an association of people who join together
second meaning: to hit with a heavy stick

explanation.surface: A trade union calls its members out on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as labour unrest; the two words are separate senses of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: A society of members is a union, and to beat someone with a cudgel is to hit or strike them.

clue.text: Ant eats crumpled paper manifest

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one word encloses the other
crumpled paper is screwed up out of shape, so its letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written, split around the other piece
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An insect chews through a scrunched-up sheet, and the damage is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manifest is clear and obvious, the same as evident or plainly visible; the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: All points bulletin

blocks.note: the four compass points, north, east, west and south

explanation.surface: An all-points bulletin is a police alert sent out everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All points bulletin' is a police phrase, but 'All points' is the four compass abbreviations in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short broadcast report of current events, which is what the word for fresh tidings names.

clue.text: Dead centre?

blocks.note: surface reading: the exact middle point of something
setter's reading: a centre, like a sports centre, set aside for the dead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead centre' is an idiom for the precise middle; read literally it is a facility for those who have died.
explanation.definitionFit: A burial ground is literally a place where deceased people are gathered, a centre for corpses.

clue.text: Information on girl in Swiss city

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone gathers details about a young woman living in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The lakeside home of many international organisations is a well-known city in Switzerland.

clue.text: He grouses about rum gun code

indicators.note: about suggests moving round and round, so the letters are turned around into a new order

blocks.note: three words whose letters are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A grumbler complains about drinking rules and weapons regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad-tempered old person who constantly complains and moans is exactly one who grouses.

clue.text: Snapping? Watch it, if it's below par!

definitions.note: the photographer's call 'watch the birdie' names the thing to watch
a phrase describing the score rather than a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: what a photographer tells people to watch while taking a snap
second meaning: a golf score of one stroke under par for a hole

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out for something that isn't up to standard.
explanation.walkthrough: Photographers once said 'watch the birdie' to make subjects look at the camera. In golf, par is the expected score for a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Old studio photographers used a toy bird to catch attention, and golfers call one stroke under par by the same name.

clue.text: Shifty fellow on foot

blocks.note: first meaning: a dishonourable, untrustworthy man
second meaning: the back part of the foot

explanation.surface: A dodgy character is on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad or scoundrel is called by this informal word, which is also the rear part of the human foot.

clue.text: Quiet sale ordered, leading to fall from grace

indicators.note: something ordered is put into a fresh arrangement, so the letters are sorted anew

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A discreet auction leads to someone's disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearrangement covers both the quiet letter and the four letters of the sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral slip or decline from previous good standing is a temporary failure of behaviour, a lapse.

clue.text: Manager gets four involved in dispatch

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: to dispatch is to kill, as an executioner does
Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A boss takes on four people to help send out deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatch' looks like sending goods, but it means kill.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior person running a company or organisation is called a manager or an executive.

clue.text: Golf club has peripheral rule for underwear

indicators.note: peripheral things lie on the edge, so only the outside letters of the next word count

blocks.note: a brassie is an old wooden golf club, roughly a two-wood
the first and last letters of rule

explanation.surface: A golf club has a dress code on the fringes about what to wear underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: A brassie is an old name for a golf club with a brass-plated sole.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra is a supporting undergarment for women, and its full formal name comes from French.

clue.text: Daughter interrupts the meal to give an award

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl breaks into a family dinner to present a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal disc presented for an achievement, as at the Olympics, is a decoration or award.

clue.text: Typical state at the time

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly
an age is a period or era

explanation.surface: A description of how things normally were in a past period.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordinary or normal, representing the usual standard, is described as average or typical.

clue.text: A bunch of video editors initially realising it's over

indicators.note: initially points to the beginnings, so only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letters of four words

explanation.surface: A team of film editors realise the project is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as finished, but the definition is the preposition meaning higher than.
explanation.definitionFit: Over and the answer are both prepositions meaning higher up than, or at a level on top of.

clue.text: Account believed and given recognition

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
to credit a story is to believe it

explanation.surface: An explanation is trusted and earns acknowledgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Officially recognised or certified as meeting required standards, a body or person becomes accredited.

clue.text: Notice a frock, in a manner of speaking

blocks.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a notice
a frock is a dress

explanation.surface: Spotting a woman's gown described in a turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb meaning spot; it is the noun for a small advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's style of delivering speech, as in a public speech, is their address or way of talking.

clue.text: Influenced, say, by leather

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word and attend to how it is pronounced, not spelt

blocks.note: to be swayed is to be influenced

explanation.surface: Someone is won over by a leather jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft leather with a napped surface, made from the underside of the skin, is suede.

clue.text: Optimistic that a mist will clear from the eye

indicators.note: when something clears from a place it leaves, so those letters are removed from the longer word

blocks.note: taken as written
a means one, written as the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hopeful that the haze will lift from someone's vision.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed string includes an extra I, because 'a' stands for one; the mist alone would leave a stray letter behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is a dated or humorous noun for the organ of sight, from the Greek word for seeing.

clue.text: Second person is unknown to the Open University

blocks.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknown quantities
the abbreviation for Britain's Open University, a distance-learning university

explanation.surface: A runner-up is a stranger to distance-learning college.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the pronoun used for the person being addressed is called the second person.

clue.text: Like raw food -- not an anagram!

blocks.note: first meaning: not heated or prepared for eating
second meaning: crossword setters say letters are cooked when they are scrambled, so letters left alone are not

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation warns solvers off rearranging; 'cooked' is slang for scrambled letters, so the reverse means left in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw food has not been through heat, and in setter's slang letters not mixed up have not been cooked either.

clue.text: Epistle re-written without postscript -- it's for the best

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken away
a piece that is re-written is set out again differently, so its letters change order

blocks.note: taken as written
PS is the abbreviation for postscript

explanation.surface: A letter is redrafted without its afterthought, which is all for the best.
explanation.definitionFit: The select group regarded as superior to the rest is the cream, the top people, the best.

clue.text: Freeze top of the milk for dessert

blocks.note: to ice is to freeze
cream rises to the top of milk

explanation.surface: Chill the creamy layer from the milk bottle to make a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet frozen confection made from dairy is a popular pudding served after a main course.

clue.text: Basic component in old school having expelled wayward Ray

indicators.note: wayward means straying off course, so the letters stray out of order
a school that has expelled someone has sent them out, so those letters leave

blocks.note: elementary school is a former name for a primary school
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An old school has thrown out an unruly pupil called Ray.
explanation.definitionFit: A fundamental part or ingredient of something is one of its elements, a basic constituent.

clue.text: Flat lay empty regularly

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving just its outer letters

blocks.note: flat ground is even
the first and last letters of lay

explanation.surface: A flat that stood unoccupied, as it did on a routine basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' could be an every-other-letter signal; here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something regularly means at uniform, steady intervals, which is the adverb for smooth uniformity.

clue.text: Ploy to show diplomacy's in charge

blocks.note: tact is diplomacy
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A scheme to prove that tactfulness is running things.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploy is a cunning manoeuvre or scheme used to achieve an end, a planned move.

clue.text: Allow convict to give up

blocks.note: a con is a convict
to cede is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: Let a prisoner surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit or grant a point in an argument is to allow it, accepting it reluctantly.

clue.text: Ancient tribe found in edifice Nigel excavated

indicators.note: found in says the letters are lying inside the words that follow
excavated means dug out, so the letters are unearthed from inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: An archaeologist named Nigel digs up traces of an old tribe in a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Boudicca led this people of East Anglia in revolt against Roman occupation of Britain.

clue.text: Some limping Bantu warriors

indicators.note: some means only part, so the letters are a portion of the next word

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: A few soldiers from southern Africa are hobbling.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi was a regiment or body of armed Zulu fighters, the Zulu being a Bantu-speaking people.

clue.text: A mongrel is irritable when given bread, they say

definitions.note: used as an adjective, of mixed breed

indicators.note: they say points to what people speak aloud, so the spelling may differ

blocks.note: cross means bad-tempered
pronounced identically to a word for raised

explanation.surface: A stray dog turns snappy when fed bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel animal comes from parents of different breeds, the product of mixed breeding.

clue.text: Provide a surfeit of teas, possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints at what the letters could become when rearranged differently

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone serves far too many cups of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To glut or satisfy completely, filling someone to excess, is to overfill them with food.

clue.text: Over 500 to 1

blocks.note: Roman numeral for five hundred
the number written as a word

explanation.surface: Betting odds of five hundred to one, as on a long shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finished or completed is said to be over, as in the game is finished.

clue.text: Crush five puerile characters with the last

indicators.note: characters means letters treated as loose tiles, free to be put down in another arrangement

blocks.note: Roman numeral for five
taken as written
the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Defeat five childish people along with the one who came last.
explanation.walkthrough: All nine letters, the numeral and the final letter included, are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce something to powder or dust by pounding is to crush or grind it.

clue.text: Mark, for example, a pair

blocks.note: first meaning: the surname of the American author Mark ...
second meaning: an old word for two

explanation.surface: A mark identifying a couple of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a sign or score, but it is a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Huckleberry Finn wrote as Mark Twain, and the archaic word for two names a couple.
